title: Light EV Retrofitting Field Manual
subtitle: Building and retrofitting e-bikes and conversion kits in developing urban markets
author: STEAM-IE Field Manual Team

pages.title: Motor Torque
pages.subtitle: How magnetic force creates wheel rotation
pages.content:
Imagine hitting a steep hill with a heavy load. Your hub motor draws max current, but excessive heat builds up rapidly inside the copper windings.

Current flowing through copper coils generates a magnetic field that pushes against permanent magnets. Higher current produces stronger rotational force, helping you climb steep inclines without stalling.

Current drives torque. Heat limits duration.
pages.imagePrompt: Cross-section diagram of a brushless hub motor showing copper windings, permanent magnets, magnetic field lines, and rotational torque vectors. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: TEST MOTOR TEMP
actionCallout.content: Touch the motor casing after a hill climb. If too hot to hold, reduce throttle.

pages.title: Battery Chemistry
pages.subtitle: Understanding lithium ion energy storage
pages.content:
Picture an unbranded battery pack bought from a local trader. Without internal balance, weak cells collapse under heavy load and ruin the entire pack.

Lithium ions shuttle between cathode and anode during charge cycles. Maintaining individual cell voltages between limits guarantees safety and extends battery lifespan significantly.

Balanced chemical reactions protect cell health.
pages.imagePrompt: Diagram showing lithium-ion cell internals with anode, cathode, electrolyte, and ion flow during charge and discharge. Technical vector diagram with clear labels, clean white background.

actionCallout.label: CHECK CELL VOLTAGE
actionCallout.content: Measure individual cell series strings with a digital multimeter before spot welding.

pages.title: Thermal Management
pages.subtitle: Dissipating heat from sealed battery enclosures
pages.content:
Consider riding through hot tropical dust with a sealed battery box. Trapped heat accelerates chemical degradation and risks thermal runaway.

Heat transfers out via conduction through aluminum casings. Adding thermal pads between cells and casing speeds transfer, keeping core temperatures safe under peak load.

Cooler operating cells last twice as long.
pages.imagePrompt: Thermal dissipation schematic of a battery pack enclosed in an aluminum box with thermal pads and heat dissipation arrows. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: ADD THERMAL PADS
actionCallout.content: Place silicone thermal pads between cell groups and the outer aluminum case.

pages.title: Energy Density
pages.subtitle: Balancing pack weight against usable capacity
pages.content:
Let's say a customer demands a 100-kilometer range on a budget bicycle frame. Overloading the frame with heavy lead batteries causes structural failure.

Lithium chemistry provides high energy per kilogram. Selecting 18650 or 21700 cells delivers maximum range while keeping total vehicle weight manageable.

Higher density means more range per kilogram.
pages.imagePrompt: Gravimetric and volumetric energy density comparison chart between Lead-Acid, NiMH, and Lithium-Ion cells. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: WEIGH YOUR PACK
actionCallout.content: Weigh cell modules before assembly to verify frame weight limits.

pages.title: Mechanical Friction
pages.subtitle: Reducing resistance in drivetrain components
pages.content:
Suppose an e-bike conversion loses 20 percent of its range instantly. Unlubricated chains and rubbing brakes waste precious battery power as heat.

Friction converts kinetic energy into useless heat energy. Aligning brake calipers and lubricating chains lowers drag, ensuring maximum motor output reaches the tire.

Free-spinning wheels save battery power.
pages.imagePrompt: Force diagram showing mechanical friction vectors on a bicycle chain, wheel bearings, and disc brake calipers. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: SPIN TEST WHEELS
actionCallout.content: Lift the bike and spin wheels by hand to confirm zero brake drag.

pages.title: Aerodynamic Drag
pages.subtitle: Air resistance forces at higher commuter speeds
pages.content:
Imagine cruising at 30 km/h into a strong headwind. Aerodynamic drag consumes power exponentially as speed increases.

Air drag quadruples every time vehicle speed doubles. Tucking wiring neatly and optimizing rider posture lowers air resistance, delivering better range at higher cruising speeds.

Lower wind profile extends high-speed range.
pages.imagePrompt: Airflow simulation diagram over an e-bike rider showing high pressure zones and turbulent wake behind rider. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: TUCK CABLING LEAN
actionCallout.content: Zip-tie loose cables flat against frame tubes to minimize wind drag.

pages.title: Regenerative Physics
pages.subtitle: Kinetic energy recovery during braking stops
pages.content:
Picture riding down a steep urban hill with constant braking. Friction brakes overheat and wear down quickly during heavy stop-and-go use.

Reversing motor magnetic poles turns kinetic motion into current. Directing generated current back to batteries slows the vehicle while recharging battery cells on downhill runs.

Braking energy feeds back into battery capacity.
pages.imagePrompt: Diagram showing power flow reversal from wheel motor through controller to battery during regenerative braking. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: ENABLE REGEN BRAKING
actionCallout.content: Configure controller e-brake inputs to trigger magnetic braking.

pages.title: Controller Setup
pages.subtitle: Matching phase wires and hall sensor signals
pages.content:
Let's say you connect a generic brushless motor controller. Incorrect phase wiring causes harsh vibration and draws high current without spinning.

The controller switches DC power to three-phase AC pulses. Matching phase color sequences and hall sensors enables smooth commutation and delivers quiet motor operation under load.

Correct signal timing eliminates motor stutter.
pages.imagePrompt: Wiring schematic connecting controller phase lines (Blue, Green, Yellow) and Hall sensor harness to brushless motor. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: MAP PHASE WIRES
actionCallout.content: Test phase combinations at low throttle until motor spins smoothly.

pages.title: BMS Configuration
pages.subtitle: Setting voltage thresholds for pack protection
pages.content:
Suppose a battery pack operates without cell monitoring. Over-discharging a single cell ruins the entire pack permanently.

The Battery Management System monitors every series group voltage. Disconnecting loads at cut-off thresholds prevents cell damage, ensuring safe charging and long overall service life.

Voltage cut-offs protect investment capital.
pages.imagePrompt: Wiring diagram of a 13S BMS connected to individual lithium cell balance leads and main power terminals. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: VERIFY BALANCE WIRES
actionCallout.content: Measure voltage on BMS balance plug harness sequentially before plugging in.

pages.title: Telemetry Sensors
pages.subtitle: Monitoring voltage and temperature in real time
pages.content:
Consider a fleet customer operating delivery e-bikes daily. Unmonitored heat buildup causes unexpected roadside failures without warning.

Digital sensors measure voltage drop, current draw, and temperature. Displaying live telemetry on handlebars warns riders early, allowing proactive maintenance before expensive component breakdown.

Live data prevents costly field breakdowns.
pages.imagePrompt: System architecture diagram showing temperature and current sensors feeding data to handlebar display unit. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: MOUNT TEMP PROBE
actionCallout.content: Attach a thermal sensor wire directly inside the motor casing.

pages.title: CAN Bus
pages.subtitle: Connecting controller BMS and digital displays
pages.content:
Imagine a tangle of fifteen individual control wires across the bike frame. Damaged individual wires cause frustrating intermittent short circuits.

Controller Area Network uses two twisted wires for all communication. Transmitting multiplexed data frames digitally cleans up wiring setups and improves system reliability in wet conditions.

Two communication wires replace complex harnesses.
pages.imagePrompt: CAN bus network wiring topology linking controller, smart BMS, display screen, and throttle unit along two wires. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: TWIST CAN WIRES
actionCallout.content: Twist CAN-High and CAN-Low signal lines together to prevent electrical noise.

pages.title: Throttle Calibration
pages.subtitle: Setting voltage thresholds for smooth startup
pages.content:
Suppose a rider twists the throttle and the e-bike jumps forward dangerously. Uncalibrated throttle response causes accidents in dense traffic.

Hall-effect throttles output 0.8V to 4.2V signals. Programming controller start thresholds above rest voltage smooths acceleration, providing predictable power control from zero speed.

Smooth voltage curves ensure safe launches.
pages.imagePrompt: Graph plotting throttle physical rotation angle against signal output voltage with controller deadband zones marked. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: SET THROTTLE DEADBAND
actionCallout.content: Adjust start voltage setting in controller software to 1.1 Volts.

pages.title: Firmware Flashing
pages.subtitle: Updating controller parameters via serial link
pages.content:
Let's say a factory controller limits motor speed artificially low. Stock settings waste potential performance under heavy cargo loads.

Connecting a USB programming cable opens internal controller registers. Flashing custom firmware parameters unlocks peak current limits, delivering custom performance matched to local terrain.

Tailored firmware optimizes motor performance.
pages.imagePrompt: Schematic showing USB-to-UART programming cable connecting computer interface to e-bike motor controller. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: BACKUP STOCK FLASH
actionCallout.content: Save original factory controller settings to computer before flashing firmware.

pages.title: Diagnostic Software
pages.subtitle: Isolating electrical fault codes rapidly
pages.content:
Picture an e-bike brought to your shop that won't turn on. Guessing faulty parts wastes valuable shop time and customer money.

Diagnostic software reads live status codes from controller inputs. Identifying broken hall sensors or blown FETs instantly pinpoint faults, ensuring fast repairs and satisfied fleet owners.

Software diagnostics shorten troubleshooting time.
pages.imagePrompt: Flowchart showing diagnostic signal path testing throttle, brake switches, BMS, and motor hall sensors. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: READ FAULT CODES
actionCallout.content: Plug diagnostic reader into main harness to scan error logs.

pages.title: Sensorless Commutating
pages.subtitle: Running motors when hall sensors fail in wet roads
pages.content:
Consider driving through heavy rain when motor hall sensors short out. Sensor failure usually strands riders stranded far from help.

Sensorless controllers measure back-electromotive force on unfed phases. Switching to back-EMF timing algorithms keeps motors running, providing reliable limpmode drive back to workshop.

Back-EMF sensing offers reliable backup operation.
pages.imagePrompt: Waveform diagram contrasting sensor-based hall signals with back-EMF voltage detection in motor controller. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: TEST SENSORLESS MODE
actionCallout.content: Unplug hall sensor harness to test controller sensorless failover drive.

pages.title: Frame Stress
pages.subtitle: Reinforcing bicycle dropouts against motor forces
pages.content:
Imagine retrofitting a powerful hub motor into standard frame dropouts. Motor axle rotation snaps thin aluminum dropouts under heavy acceleration.

Torque forces push in reverse against axle slots. Installing thick steel torque arms transfers forces safely onto frame tubes, keeping wheels securely mounted under max torque.

Torque arms prevent frame dropout failure.
pages.imagePrompt: Stress distribution diagram on bicycle rear dropout under motor torque load with torque arm installed. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: FIT TORQUE ARMS
actionCallout.content: Bolt a 4mm stainless steel torque arm to axle flat and frame.

pages.title: Axle Alignment
pages.subtitle: Ensuring straight tracking under heavy loading
pages.content:
Suppose a retrofitted cargo bike pulls heavily to the left. Misassembled wheel axles cause rapid tire wear and dangerous handling.

Precision axle seating centers wheels inside frame chainstays. Using alignment washers and torque wrenches fixes axle positions, ensuring straight tracking and balanced brake pad contact.

Aligned axles improve handling and tire life.
pages.imagePrompt: Top-down engineering view of bicycle frame chainstays showing axle alignment washers and wheel centerline. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: MEASURE AXLE GAP
actionCallout.content: Measure distance from rim to frame chainstays on both sides equally.

pages.title: Brake Sizing
pages.subtitle: Upgrading mechanical stoppers for heavy e-bikes
pages.content:
Let's say a fast e-bike relies on cheap rim brakes. Standard rubber pads overheat and fade instantly at higher electric speeds.

Higher speed and weight demand greater heat dissipation. Fitting 180mm hydraulic disc rotors increases leverage and cooling surface, delivering short stopping distances under heavy load.

Larger rotors stop heavy electric bikes safely.
pages.imagePrompt: Mechanical comparison diagram showing brake leverage and heat dissipation area between 160mm and 180mm disc rotors. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: INSTALL DISC ROTORS
actionCallout.content: Upgrade front brake setup to 180mm rotor with metallic brake pads.

pages.title: Wiring Harness
pages.subtitle: Building waterproof custom main electrical harnesses
pages.content:
Picture electrical connections wrapped in cheap electrical tape. Water penetrates tape joints causing corrosion and intermittent electrical shorts.

Waterproof connectors seal wiring against rain and road spray. Crimping Julet or Higigo sealed plugs isolates internal pins, building weatherproof wiring harnesses built for long outdoor life.

Sealed connectors prevent rain-induced wiring failures.
pages.imagePrompt: Cutaway illustration of a waterproof Julet electrical connector showing rubber O-ring seal and crimped pins. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: SEAL WIRE JOINTS
actionCallout.content: Use adhesive-lined heat shrink tubing over every soldered wire connection.

pages.title: Drivetrain Gearing
pages.subtitle: Matching motor RPM to human cadence limits
pages.content:
Suppose a mid-drive kit spins pedals too fast for comfort. Inappropriate gear ratios cause rider legs to spin out quickly.

Mid-drives multiply torque through rear cassette gears. Selecting appropriate front chainring teeth counts balances motor power and human cadence, providing efficient climbing and comfortable cruising speeds.

Optimal gearing maximizes mid-drive motor efficiency.
pages.imagePrompt: Drivetrain schematic illustrating front chainring, chain path, rear cassette cogs, and cadence torque interaction. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: SWAP CHAINRING SIZE
actionCallout.content: Install a 42-tooth narrow-wide front chainring for mid-drive setups.

pages.title: Suspension Geometry
pages.subtitle: Absorbing road impact to protect mounted electronics
pages.content:
Consider driving an un-suspended retrofitted bike over unpaved rough roads. Severe vibration cracks solder joints and cell tabs over time.

Suspension forks absorb high-frequency road shocks. Adjusting fork preload and rebound damping dampens vibrations, protecting sensitive batteries and electronics from physical vibration damage.

Suspension shields battery assemblies from road shock.
pages.imagePrompt: Engineering schematic of bicycle front suspension fork showing coil spring, oil damper, and travel vector. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: SET FORK PRELOAD
actionCallout.content: Adjust suspension fork sag to 20 percent total travel under weight.

pages.title: Enclosure Sealing
pages.subtitle: Protecting battery cases against dust and water
pages.content:
Imagine fine road dust penetrating a custom battery box. Dust accumulation creates conductive bridges across cells causing short circuits.

Gaskets seal enclosure seams against particulate entry. Applying neoprene foam gaskets and IP65 glands blocks dust and water ingress, maintaining clean dry environment inside battery boxes.

Gasket seals defend electronics from weather.
pages.imagePrompt: Cross-section drawing of aluminum enclosure lid with neoprene gasket seal and IP65 cable gland assembly. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: FIT GLAND NUTS
actionCallout.content: Install IP65 cable glands for all wires exiting battery enclosures.

pages.title: Structural Welding
pages.subtitle: Fabricating custom steel mounting brackets safely
pages.content:
Suppose a weak welded battery mount snaps while riding fast over bumps. Falling battery packs cause dangerous crashes and instant destruction.

Proper welding penetrates deep into base metal joint surfaces. Using TIG or MIG welding on mild steel builds rigid brackets, providing rock-solid mount points for heavy custom batteries.

Deep weld penetration prevents structural bracket failures.
pages.imagePrompt: Diagram showing correct TIG weld bead profile and penetration depth on steel frame tubing joint. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: INSPECT WELD JOINTS
actionCallout.content: Stress test custom battery brackets with heavy rubber mallet before mounting.

pages.title: Torque Arms
pages.subtitle: Preventing dropout shear in conversion kits
pages.content:
Let's say a conversion kit motor spins loose inside frame dropouts. Sheared motor wires destroy expensive controllers instantly when axle spins.

Torque arms anchor flat axle ends directly to sturdy frame tubes. Clamping stainless steel torque arms firmly handles rotational force, keeping axles stationary and wiring completely safe.

Sturdy torque arms prevent catastrophic axle rotation.
pages.imagePrompt: Detailed assembly view of two-piece adjustable stainless steel torque arm clamped to frame stays. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: TORQUE AXLE NUTS
actionCallout.content: Tighten motor axle nuts to 45 Newton-meters using calibrated torque wrench.

pages.title: Ergonomic Design
pages.subtitle: Arranging handlebar controls for comfortable operation
pages.content:
Picture a rider straining thumbs to reach throttle and brake levers. Poor control placement causes rider fatigue and slow reaction times.

Ergonomic control layouts place levers within easy thumb reach. Angling throttle buttons and brake levers naturally improves rider comfort, enabling fast emergency braking response in city traffic.

Intuitive control placement increases rider safety.
pages.imagePrompt: Handlebar control layout diagram showing optimal reach zones and angles for throttle, display, and brakes. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: ANGLE LEVERS NATURAL
actionCallout.content: Set brake lever angle to 45 degrees downward inline with arms.

pages.title: Cable Routing
pages.subtitle: Running clean wiring channels along frame tubes
pages.content:
Consider an e-bike conversion with dangling loose wire loops. Loose wires snag on branches and look unprofessional to paying customers.

Clean cable routing follows primary frame structural lines. Securing wires using spiral wrap and cable guides tidies visual presentation, creating clean factory-looking builds that command premium prices.

Clean cable management creates professional aesthetics.
pages.imagePrompt: Bicycle frame diagram highlighting neatly routed wire paths using frame guides and spiral wrap hose. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: WRAP CABLE HOSE
actionCallout.content: Encase loose handlebar control wires into spiral protective hose wrap.

pages.title: Frame Painting
pages.subtitle: Applying durable finishes to retrofitted frames
pages.content:
Imagine bare steel welds rusting after first monsoon rainstorm. Unprotected metal degrades quickly and looks unattractive to buyers.

Surface preparation and primer coat protect raw metal underneath. Spraying tough polyurethane enamel topcoats blocks humidity, delivering glossy durable finishes that resist scratching daily.

Quality paint seals metal against corrosion rust.
pages.imagePrompt: Layered cutaway diagram showing steel tube, etch primer, base coat, and clear polyurethane coat. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: SAND RAW METAL
actionCallout.content: Sand welded frame joints with 320 grit paper before applying primer.

pages.title: Custom Badging
pages.subtitle: Building brand recognition on converted e-bikes
pages.content:
Suppose your workshop conversions look like unbranded generic machines. Unbranded products fail to build workshop reputation locally.

Custom badges communicate local craft quality and pride. Applying vinyl headtube logos and branding graphics establishes visual identity, helping generate word-of-mouth referral sales in your city.

Branded frames establish professional business identity.
pages.imagePrompt: Graphic design placement guide showing logo badge positioning on headtube and frame downtube. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: APPLY LOGO BADGE
actionCallout.content: Place waterproof branded vinyl decal on bicycle headtube centered straight.

pages.title: Lighting Placement
pages.subtitle: Positioning headlamps for night urban visibility
pages.content:
Consider riding home after dark on poorly lit streets. Low-mounted headlights project harsh shadows hiding deep road potholes.

Proper headlight height casts wide illumination across road paths. Mounting high-lumen LED lights on fork crowns illuminates obstacles clearly, ensuring safe night navigation for delivery riders.

Strategic light placement improves night road visibility.
pages.imagePrompt: Optical light beam projection diagram showing headlight beam pattern cut-off angle and ground coverage. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: AIM HEADLIGHT BEAM
actionCallout.content: Aim headlight beam slightly downward to avoid blinding oncoming traffic.

pages.title: Cargo Bay Design
pages.subtitle: Designing practical visual layouts for cargo storage
pages.content:
Let's say a local bakery needs custom cargo boxes on trikes. Bulky ugly boxes ruin vehicle balance and visual appeal.

Balanced proportions harmonize cargo box geometry with frame lines. Using lightweight composite panels and clean vinyl graphics blends function and style, creating eye-catching mobile advertising for commercial fleet clients.

Attractive cargo boxes serve as rolling billboards.
pages.imagePrompt: Side elevation drawing of e-cargo bike with integrated box dimensions, branding area, and center of gravity marked. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: MOCKUP CARGO BOX
actionCallout.content: Build cardboard box mockup on frame to check leg clearance before fabrication.

pages.title: Range Calculation
pages.subtitle: Estimating travel distance per battery charge
pages.content:
Imagine promising a customer 50 kilometers range on a tiny battery pack. Underestimating energy consumption leaves customers stranded mid-trip.

Energy consumed equals watt-hours divided by average speed and terrain drag. Calculating battery capacity in Watt-Hours predicts real-world range, delivering accurate distance figures customers can rely on.

Watt-hours divided by efficiency equals true range.
pages.imagePrompt: Mathematical formula diagram calculating total Watt-Hours from Voltage and Amp-Hour ratings. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: CALCULATE PACK WATT-HOURS
actionCallout.content: Multiply battery voltage by amp-hours to find total energy capacity.

pages.title: Gear Ratios
pages.subtitle: Calculating torque multiplication for steep hills
pages.content:
Suppose a mid-drive motor overheats trying to climb steep gradients. Wrong gear ratios strain motors past thermal limits continuously.

Gear ratio equals chainring teeth divided by rear cog teeth count. Selecting a high mechanical reduction ratio multiplies wheel climbing torque, allowing cool motor operation up steep city hills.

Higher numerical gear ratios increase torque output.
pages.imagePrompt: Gear ratio chart plotting front chainring and rear cog teeth combinations against mechanical leverage. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: COMPUTE GEAR RATIO
actionCallout.content: Divide front chainring teeth count by largest rear cassette cog teeth.

pages.title: Battery Sizing
pages.subtitle: Calculating series and parallel cell configurations
pages.content:
Picture building a custom 48V battery from loose 18650 cells. Incorrect series cell counts cause wrong pack voltage output.

Series cells multiply voltage while parallel cells multiply current capacity. Configuring 13 series and 4 parallel cells builds a 48V 12Ah pack, delivering exact voltage and capacity for target motors.

Series sets voltage. Parallel sets current capacity.
pages.imagePrompt: Cell matrix schematic showing 13S4P lithium pack wiring with series parallel connections labeled clearly. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: COUNT CELL MATRIX
actionCallout.content: Multiply series cell count by nominal cell voltage to check target.

pages.title: Payload Capacity
pages.subtitle: Calculating total weight limits for safe transport
pages.content:
Consider loading 150 kilograms onto a standard commuter conversion frame. Exceeding structural payload ratings causes frame failure suddenly.

Total payload includes rider weight plus freight cargo combined. Calculating frame stress limits and spoke tension establishes safe limits, keeping cargo transport operations stable and break-free.

Respect weight limits to protect structural frame.
pages.imagePrompt: Payload breakdown diagram illustrating rider mass, cargo mass, frame load points, and maximum vector limits. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: SUM TOTAL PAYLOAD
actionCallout.content: Add weight of rider, cargo box, and battery to verify frame rating.

pages.title: Voltage Drop
pages.subtitle: Calculating power loss across thin wiring runs
pages.content:
Suppose you use thin 18-gauge wire for main battery power lines. Thin wires cause severe voltage drop and heat under current.

Wire resistance wastes power as heat proportional to length and current. Selecting thick 12-gauge copper wire conductors minimizes voltage drop, ensuring full battery power reaches motor controllers directly.

Thicker power cables eliminate energy voltage losses.
pages.imagePrompt: Graph plotting wire gauge thickness against voltage drop over two meters length at 30 Amps current. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: CHECK WIRE RESISTANCE
actionCallout.content: Measure voltage drop across power leads under full motor throttle load.

pages.title: C-Rate Dynamics
pages.subtitle: Calculating peak discharge currents during startup
pages.content:
Let's say a motor draws 30 Amps from a small 10Ah battery pack. Exceeding maximum cell C-rate overheats cells quickly.

Discharge C-rate measures current draw relative to pack capacity. Selecting 3C continuous rated lithium cells handles 30 Amp bursts safely, delivering strong launch power without damaging cell internal structure.

High C-rate cells handle heavy acceleration currents.
pages.imagePrompt: Formula diagram showing calculation of max discharge Amps from cell C-rate and Amp-Hour capacity. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: MULTIPLY CELL C-RATE
actionCallout.content: Multiply cell Ah capacity by continuous C-rate to find max continuous current.

pages.title: Spokes Tensioning
pages.subtitle: Calculating spoke tension vectors on heavy hub motors
pages.content:
Picture heavy hub motor wheels wobbling after two weeks of riding. Uneven spoke tension snaps spokes under motor torque loads.

Spokes transmit rotational motor torque from hub shell to rim. Balancing tension to 1100 Newtons evenly distributes mechanical loads, building durable hub motor wheels that stay true indefinitely.

Equal spoke tension builds durable motor wheels.
pages.imagePrompt: Wheel dish vector diagram showing spoke angle, tension force vectors, and hub motor shell alignment. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: MEASURE SPOKE TENSION
actionCallout.content: Use a spoke tension meter to verify uniform tension across all spokes.

pages.title: Second-Life Cells
pages.subtitle: Testing and re-sorting laptop batteries economically
pages.content:
Imagine new lithium cells costing more than your customer's budget. Buying untested recycled cells risks pack short circuits easily.

Testing measures true internal resistance and capacity of used cells. Sorting recycled cells with identical capacity builds cheap reliable second-life packs, opening affordable e-bike mobility for low-income city commuters.

Capacity matched recycled cells cut battery costs.
pages.imagePrompt: Process flowchart showing testing, capacity grading, and sorting recycled 18650 cells for reassembly. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: TEST CELL CAPACITY
actionCallout.content: Discharge test second-life cells on a digital capacity tester before building.

pages.title: Solar Canopy
pages.subtitle: Mounting light solar roofs on cargo trikes
pages.content:
Consider grid power outages stopping delivery fleet charging overnight. Dead batteries stall business delivery operations completely next morning.

Solar panels charge batteries continuously while parked outdoors in daylight. Mounting a 100W flexible solar canopy adds 15 kilometers free range daily, providing off-grid charging capability during frequent urban power blackouts.

Solar canopies supply free daytime trickle charge.
pages.imagePrompt: System diagram showing flexible solar panel on cargo roof connected through MPPT solar controller to battery. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: CONNECT MPPT CHARGER
actionCallout.content: Install a step-up solar MPPT charger between roof panel and battery.

pages.title: Regenerative Braking
pages.subtitle: Adapting simple e-brakes to capture downhill power
pages.content:
Suppose hilly terrain drains e-bike batteries before daily work finishes. Standard mechanical braking wastes all downhill kinetic energy as friction.

Electronic braking switches trigger controller regenerative routines automatically. Capturing kinetic energy during long downhill runs recovers up to 10 percent range, extending daily operating hours without extra battery weight.

Downhill kinetic recovery stretches daily range.
pages.imagePrompt: Circuit diagram connecting brake lever microswitch to controller e-brake signal input wire. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: WIRE E-BRAKE SWITCH
actionCallout.content: Wire brake lever magnetic cutoff switch directly into controller e-brake pins.

pages.title: Local Material
pages.subtitle: Using local scrap steel for custom mounting plates
pages.content:
Imagine waiting six weeks for imported aluminum motor mounting brackets. Import shipping delays halt workshop production lines and sales.

Local steel scrap provides cheap malleable raw material instantly. Cutting and drilling local 3mm steel plate builds custom motor mounts locally, keeping conversion work moving without dependence on foreign suppliers.

Local steel fabrication eliminates import waiting times.
pages.imagePrompt: Engineering template drawing for cutting e-bike battery mounting plate from sheet steel. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: DRILL STEEL BRACKET
actionCallout.content: Cut battery mounting plate from 3mm local steel scrap using angle grinder.

pages.title: Modular Frame
pages.subtitle: Building bolt-on conversion subframes for bikes
pages.content:
Picture cutting or welding customer bicycle frames permanently. Permanent frame modifications weaken steel tubing structural integrity.

Modular bolt-on subframes clamp securely onto standard bicycle frames. Designing clamping brackets that wrap frame tubes supports heavy motors, enabling clean reversible e-bike conversions without damaging base bikes.

Bolt-on subframes preserve original bicycle frames.
pages.imagePrompt: Exploded assembly view of bolt-on steel subframe clamping onto standard bicycle bottom bracket. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: CLAMP SUBFRAME MOUNT
actionCallout.content: Tighten rubber-lined hose clamps around subframe frame contact points.

pages.title: Mid-Drive Adapters
pages.subtitle: Fitting conversion kits onto non-standard bottom brackets
pages.content:
Let's say a customer bicycle has a wider bottom bracket shell. Standard mid-drive kits fail to fit wider shells properly.

Custom spacer adapters bridge wider bottom bracket dimensions cleanly. Machining custom threaded aluminum adapter rings centers mid-drive shafts, allowing mid-drive conversions on unusual mountain or cargo frames.

Custom adapters adapt mid-drives to any frame.
pages.imagePrompt: Cross-section schematic of threaded bottom bracket shell adapter ring fitting mid-drive motor shaft. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: MEASURE SHELL WIDTH
actionCallout.content: Measure bottom bracket shell width using calipers before ordering adapter rings.

pages.title: Target Market
pages.subtitle: Identifying high-mileage urban delivery workers
pages.content:
Suppose you spend marketing effort targeting casual weekend riders. Low-usage customers rarely buy conversions or ongoing repairs.

Commercial delivery riders need cheap fast transportation daily. Targeting high-mileage couriers and local traders solves their high fuel expenses, creating eager buyers who value fast return on investment.

High-mileage riders profit most from electric conversions.
pages.imagePrompt: Customer segmentation chart comparing daily mileage and fuel savings between commuters and delivery riders. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: INTERVIEW LOCAL COURIERS
actionCallout.content: Ask three local delivery riders their daily fuel spend to demonstrate savings.

pages.title: Pricing Strategy
pages.subtitle: Structuring competitive conversion kit pricing packages
pages.content:
Imagine pricing conversions too close to new imported factory e-bikes. High prices discourage budget-conscious local commuters instantly.

Cost-plus pricing adds fair labor margins over raw part costs. Offering tiered kit packages from basic to heavy-duty fits varied budgets, capturing broad market share across different income levels.

Tiered kit options attract diverse customer budgets.
pages.imagePrompt: Tiered pricing comparison table detailing basic hub kit, mid-range kit, and heavy-duty cargo kit options. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: CALCULATE KIT MARGIN
actionCallout.content: Add 30 percent labor margin over raw kit component costs.

pages.title: Unit Economics
pages.subtitle: Tracking direct part and labor costs per build
pages.content:
Consider selling conversions without calculating exact individual part costs. Hidden shipping and small parts consume all profit margins.

Unit economics breaks down motor, battery, wiring, and labor costs. Subtracting direct costs from conversion selling prices reveals gross margin, ensuring every build generates predictable profit for your workshop.

Track component costs to guarantee profit margins.
pages.imagePrompt: Unit economics cost breakdown stack showing parts, labor, overhead, and profit margin per build. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: ITEMIZE BUILD COSTS
actionCallout.content: List cost of motor, battery, controller, connectors, and labor on paper.

pages.title: Break-Even Point
pages.subtitle: Calculating monthly builds needed to cover rent
pages.content:
Suppose shop rent and electricity bills accumulate every month. Unplanned fixed overhead expenses drain personal savings fast.

Break-even divides monthly fixed costs by profit margin per build. Calculating exact monthly conversion targets sets clear operational goals, ensuring shop revenue consistently covers overhead costs safely.

Fixed overhead divided by margin equals break-even units.
pages.imagePrompt: Break-even chart plotting fixed monthly costs against cumulative conversion profit lines. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: FIND BREAK-EVEN UNITS
actionCallout.content: Divide total monthly shop rent by profit earned per e-bike conversion.

pages.title: Working Capital
pages.subtitle: Managing inventory cash for motors and battery cells
pages.content:
Imagine tying up all workshop cash buying ten unused motors. Lack of cash prevents buying urgent replacement parts needed now.

Working capital manages cash flow between buying inventory and sales. Ordering parts only upon customer deposit receipt protects cash reserves, keeping your micro-workshop solvent and agile during quiet months.

Require customer deposits to fund part purchases.
pages.imagePrompt: Cash flow cycle diagram illustrating cash conversion timeline from parts purchase to final customer payment. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: COLLECT PART DEPOSITS
actionCallout.content: Require 50 percent advance deposit before ordering conversion kit parts.

pages.title: Cash Flow
pages.subtitle: Maintaining positive daily workshop cash balances
pages.content:
Picture delivering finished e-bikes on credit to friends. Delayed customer payments prevent paying shop rent on time.

Strict payment terms demand full balance payment upon final pickup. Maintaining positive daily cash flow funds shop operations continuously, building stable financial foundation for future business expansion.

Cash upon delivery keeps shop operations solvent.
pages.imagePrompt: Monthly cash flow forecast chart showing incoming customer payments versus outgoing operational expenses. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: ENFORCE CASH ON DELIVERY
actionCallout.content: Hand over keys only after full final payment balance clears.

pages.title: Fleet Service
pages.subtitle: Selling recurring monthly maintenance to delivery fleets
pages.content:
Consider relying solely on one-off conversion sales for income. Inconsistent monthly sales create unpredictable workshop revenue streams.

Fleet maintenance contracts offer monthly inspection and repair services. Charging flat monthly subscription fees per vehicle secures steady income, ensuring predictable monthly revenue and long-term customer partnerships.

Recurring service contracts stabilize workshop monthly income.
pages.imagePrompt: Contract service workflow diagram outlining monthly safety check, battery test, and brake adjustment routine. Technical vector diagram, clean lines, white background.

actionCallout.label: OFFER SERVICE CONTRACTS
actionCallout.content: Propose flat monthly service plans to local delivery fleet operators.
